chapters.heading: UNITED STATES CAPITOL POLICE REFORM AND ACCOUNTABILITY

sections.heading: Emergency authority, lockdowns, and evacuations
paragraphs: (a) The Chief may take immediate action necessary to protect Congress, Members of Congress, officers of Congress, congressional employees, witnesses, invited guests, visitors, congressional proceedings, and the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds during an emergency.

(b) An emergency may include violence, an imminent threat of violence, fire, explosion, hazardous material, medical emergency, riot, unlawful entry, active obstruction of congressional business, credible threat against a Member of Congress, credible threat against a congressional proceeding, security breach, natural disaster, or any other condition requiring immediate action to protect life, property, or the functioning of Congress.

(c) During an emergency, the Chief may order a lockdown, evacuation, shelter-in-place, temporary closure, restricted access area, security perimeter, controlled entry point, suspension of public access, emergency deployment, protective movement, or other temporary security measure necessary to respond to the emergency.
(d) A lockdown, evacuation, or emergency closure affecting a House-controlled area shall be coordinated with the House Sergeant at Arms as soon as practicable.
(e) A lockdown, evacuation, or emergency closure affecting a Senate-controlled area shall be coordinated with the Senate Sergeant at Arms as soon as practicable.

(f) A lockdown, evacuation, or emergency closure affecting both Houses, a joint session, a shared congressional area, or the general security of the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds shall be reported to the Capitol Police Board as soon as practicable.

(g) The Capitol Police may act without prior approval of the Board, the Speaker, the President pro tempore, or either Sergeant at Arms where delay would endanger life, permit serious injury, allow violence to continue, expose Congress to an imminent threat, or prevent officers from securing an active emergency.

(h) Emergency authority under this section shall be limited to the time, place, and measures reasonably necessary to address the emergency, protect persons, secure property, preserve evidence, restore order, or return control to the lawful authority ordinarily responsible for the affected space.

(i) An emergency measure shall not be continued after the emergency basis for the measure has ended, except where continuation is approved by the Board or by the relevant House authority for a specific and continuing security reason.
(j) The Chief shall ensure that officers are informed of the scope, purpose, duration, and access rules of any lockdown, evacuation, restricted area, or emergency closure where practicable.

(k) The Capitol Police may assist Members of Congress, officers of Congress, congressional employees, witnesses, invited guests, and visitors during an evacuation, shelter-in-place, emergency movement, or protective relocation.

(l) The Capitol Police may deny entry to, remove, detain, or arrest a person during an emergency where such action is authorized by this Act and necessary to secure the emergency scene, protect persons, prevent obstruction, enforce a lawful evacuation or lockdown order, or stop a violation of law. (m)The Chief may request assistance from another lawful authority during an emergency where additional personnel, equipment, expertise, transportation, medical response, fire response, explosive response, intelligence, or other support is necessary to protect Congress or restore order.

(n) Any emergency action involving a lockdown, evacuation, outside agency assistance, use of force, arrest, detention, injury, death, major property damage, or substantial interruption of congressional business shall be documented by the Chief as soon as practicable after the emergency permits.

(o) The report shall state the nature of the emergency, the authority relied upon, the actions taken, the persons or areas affected, the duration of the emergency measure, the officers and outside agencies involved, any arrests or detentions, any use of force, any injuries or property damage, and any continuing security concern.

(p) Emergency authority shall not be used to prevent a lawful vote, delay a proceeding for political reasons, deny access to a Member of Congress for a non-security purpose, suppress lawful debate, or interfere with the constitutional authority of either House.

sections.heading: Political neutrality and prohibited uses
paragraphs: (a) The Capitol Police shall perform its duties in a neutral, lawful, and nonpartisan manner.

(b) No officer, employee, special officer, policy, regulation, order, deployment, investigation, arrest, detention, removal, access rule, protective service, emergency action, or security measure may be used for the purpose of favoring or disfavoring any political party, caucus, faction, Member of Congress, officer of Congress, nominee, witness, employee, ideology, viewpoint, legislative position, or lawful political activity.

(c) The Capitol Police shall not interfere with debate, voting, committee work, legislative negotiations, oversight activity, witness testimony, congressional investigations, or any other lawful function of Congress except where action is necessary to protect life, prevent injury, stop violence, enforce lawful access rules, respond to an emergency, prevent obstruction of proceedings, or carry out a lawful order under this Act.

(d) The Capitol Police shall not be used to intimidate a Member of Congress, officer of Congress, employee of Congress, witness, invited guest, or visitor because of testimony, voting, debate, speech, association, political position, party affiliation, or participation in a congressional proceeding.

(e) The Capitol Police shall not monitor, investigate, collect information on, or maintain records concerning lawful political activity, legislative activity, speech, association, protest, press activity, or public criticism unless such activity is directly connected to a credible threat, violation of law, obstruction of congressional business, security incident, protective assignment, or other lawful duty of the Capitol Police.

(f) No officer or employee of the Capitol Police may knowingly execute an order that is plainly unlawful, issued for a political purpose, or intended to interfere with the lawful proceedings, privileges, or functions of either House.

(g) An officer or employee who receives an order that appears to be unlawful, politically motivated, retaliatory, or inconsistent with this Act may report the order to a supervisor, the Chief, the relevant Sergeant at Arms, the Board, or any committee or officer authorized by either House.

(h) No person may retaliate against an officer, employee, special officer, complainant, witness, Member of Congress, officer of Congress, or congressional employee for reporting misuse of the Capitol Police, refusing to carry out an unlawful order, cooperating with an investigation, filing a complaint, preserving evidence, or providing information to the Board or either House.

(i) The Chief shall issue regulations requiring officers and employees of the Capitol Police to receive training on political neutrality, member privileges, lawful orders, prohibited retaliation, protection of congressional proceedings, and the limits of Capitol Police authority.

(j) The Chief shall investigate credible allegations that the Capitol Police, or any officer, employee, special officer, policy, deployment, investigation, or security action, has been used for a political, retaliatory, personal, or unlawful purpose.

(k) A violation of this section may result in discipline, removal from assignment, suspension of authority, termination, referral to the Board, referral to either House, referral for prosecution where appropriate, or any other lawful corrective action.

(l) The Board may review any allegation involving political misuse, retaliation, executive interference, interference with a congressional proceeding, discrimination between Members, or misuse of Capitol Police authority against a witness, nominee, officer, employee, or visitor. (m)The Chief shall maintain records of complaints, investigations, findings, and corrective actions involving alleged violations of this section. Records may be maintained in closed form where necessary to protect personnel information, security information, classified information, private personal information, or an active investigation.
